Oldest of four; younger siblings Maggie, Paul, Raymond; two brothers now deceased
Father - machine operator at Bohn Aluminum and Brass (Adrian), die-cast machine, UAW, 1938-1969; 8th-grade education

Mother - homemaker; WWII Rosie-the-Riveter at Willow Run bomber plant (1942-1945), B-24 Liberator wing panels, bus commute Adrian-Ypsilanti 1 hour each way, 3 rotating shifts; high-school 1933 education; kept Willow Run ID card her whole life
Grandfather Otto immigrated from Baden, Germany pre-WWI; trade unionist
Graduated Adrian High 1958; attended Siena Heights 1958-1960 (business administration, did not finish)
Grandmother Elsa (mother's mother) lived with family 1953-1961
Career crossroads 1960: Sister Mary Agnes encouraged CPA path; chose marriage
Marriage to Harold Cintron, 1961; 58-year marriage
Move to Saline 1964; home purchase for $14,000 (supervisor of Harold recommended the town)
Children's births: Kathy 1962, Daniel 1964, Rebecca 1968
Father died 1974
One night class at Washtenaw Community College, 1974
Harold quit smoking cold turkey 1979 after his father's lung cancer death
Uncle Walter (mother's brother) died of cirrhosis 1982 - cautionary tale re: drinking
Son Daniel came out in 1986 (age 22); parents supported him, marched in Detroit Pride 1990 (Harold in Tigers cap)
One speeding ticket 1978 on M-52 outside Chelsea
1987 break-in attempt at home - Harold scared intruder off with flashlight
Daniel's 1993 US-12 rear-end accident - state trooper was kind
Mortgage paid off 1999 (Rebecca's college graduation year)
Breast cancer Stage 1, 2005 - lumpectomy + radiation
Daniel's marriage to Marco, 2015
Re-registered as political Independent, 2016
Harold's death (heart attack), September 14, 2019 - Saline officer performed CPR; defining loss; 'hum went'; still sets out 2 coffee cups some mornings
Adopted cat Winston from Humane Society, 2020 (post-widowhood companion)
Brian-Keisha marriage 2021 - catalyst for cross-cultural learning
George Floyd video 2020 - cried watching it; thought about Daniel; shifted listening
Cataract surgery both eyes, 2022
Sister Maggie diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer's, 2023
Fall on ice January 2024 - bruised hip, no fracture; wake-up call re: driveway plow
Depressive stretch February 2025 (anniversary grief); Kathy stayed 2 nights, cleaned out Harold's workshop together - turning point
Bronchitis November 2025
End-of-life fears: being a burden; losing mind like Maggie; not afraid of death itself

media_and_information_diet.summary: Deliberately curated, relatively narrow, high-credibility media diet heavy on public-service journalism and local print. Trusts PBS NewsHour, Meet the Press, Face the Nation, Ann Arbor News online, Saline Reporter print, Consumer Reports, CDC.gov, and Wall Street Journal opinion page (occasionally). Explicitly rejects Fox News as 'not serious' and is actively critical of Facebook-driven misinformation, having personally pushed back against church friends sharing false content.

summaries.demographer: Deeva Cintron is an 85-year-old (DOB 1940-06-11) non-Hispanic White, German-English heritage, widowed woman (Q84-Q89) with 'some college' educational attainment from a two-year 1958-1960 business-administration program at Siena Heights University (Q01, Q90). She has lived continuously in Saline, MI 48176 since 1964, owning a mortgage-free single-family home on a 1/3-acre lot (Q08, Q58). Household is single-person post-widowhood (Harold d. 2019-09-14), with one companion animal (Q11); three adult children and six grandchildren live nonlocally in Ann Arbor, Portland OR, Toledo, Denver, Grand Valley, and Bowling Green (Q05). Household income is ~$5,500/month gross from a UAW Ford pension, her own and survivor Social Security, and investment RMDs (Q72-Q74), placing her above regional senior median. Life-course profile: stable long-term marriage (58 years), three children born 1962-1968, long-resident homeowner, post-retirement civic actor - a textbook stable-Midwestern-widow demographic archetype.
summaries.behavioral_economist: Cintron exhibits extreme loss aversion and a strong preference for predictability manifested as a rigid daily schedule (5:45-wake, 6-p.m.-dinner, 9:30-lights-out), redundant financial controls (online bill-pay backed by a handwritten spiral-notebook register, Q17, Q56), and strict no-debt posture (Q63). Time preferences are unusually low-discount / long-horizon: house paid off in 1999 via decades of below-means living (Q58, Q83), emergency fund ($42K at Bank of Ann Arbor) maintained with zero slack tolerance - a $380 furnace repair was replenished in two months by reducing fabric spending (Q60). Identity-signaling behaviors cluster around thrift, reliability, and order ('a person's word was their bond,' Q24; 'measure a board four times before cutting,' Q03). Response to peer influence is selective: she actively resists schedule-disruption norms but demonstrates flexibility in value-updating when triggered by in-group authority (Sister Mary Agnes, grandson's spouse Keisha). She also shows classic reciprocal altruism in tithing ($200/month), NAACP giving, and annual gift-tax-exclusion transfers (Q56, Q62, Q27). Risk posture is conservative but not paralyzed - she adopted Zoom, QuickBooks, and a CGM only after trusted-agent mediation.
summaries.political_scientist: Cintron is a high-frequency, high-engagement civic actor: ~120 elections voted (Q23), 8 cycles as a Saline precinct-3 election worker 2004-2018, lifelong church treasurer, and senior-center volunteer bookkeeper. Her party identification has trajectory from lifelong Republican (voted Eisenhower-through-both-Bushes) through Obama-2008 defection, 2016 re-registration as Independent, and current weak-to-moderate Democratic lean for federal races with split-ticket local voting (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). Institutional trust is differentiated and high-resolution: strong for local police (Q20), PBS, CDC, and mainline Protestant institutions (Q42, Q47); declining for Republican party-as-institution since 2010/2016 (Q25); critical of Facebook information environment (Q48); rejects Fox News as 'not serious.' Community attachment is extraordinarily deep - 62-year home tenure, 61-year church membership, 50+-year local friendships - making her a textbook case of stable local social-capital accumulation. Policy preferences are cross-cutting: fiscally conservative, pro-Social-Security/Medicare, pro-balanced-budget, pro-background-checks, pro-choice (privately), pro-marriage-equality (personal stake via son), pro-NAACP donation, stewardship-framed environmentalism - a coherent Rockefeller-Republican-to-moderate-Democrat migration narrative.
summaries.psychologist: Cintron presents a high-conscientiousness, moderate-neuroticism, moderate-introversion personality with strong need-for-order and an explicitly competitive streak (seed) expressed socially through bridge and precision-crafts rather than overt assertion. Self-describes as a 'functional worrier' (Q45) with episodic depressive symptomatology - grief-anchored February 2025 episode (Q44), anniversary-linked seasonal low mood, mild health-and-driving anxiety - uncoupled from formal psychiatric diagnosis or pharmacotherapy and managed via stoic, behavioral, faith-based, and relational coping rather than clinical care (consistent with her birth-cohort help-seeking norms, Q44). Emotional regulation strategy is ritualized: rigid schedule, daily gardening, morning prayer, 3-p.m. tea, and evening knitting operate as self-soothing infrastructure. Self-concept is value-rank-ordered (family > word > order > service > faith > perspective, Q109) and coherent. Relational style is securely attached with dense, long-duration ties and explicit value-updating following high-trust family contact (Daniel coming out in 1986; grandson Brian's 2021 interracial marriage triggered engagement with BLM issues, Q26-Q28). Cognitive style is detail-oriented and verificationist - double-checks crosswords and ledgers (seed; Q03, Q56) - with metacognitive awareness of her own rigidity and stated effort to 'honor Harold's teasing' by loosening. Motivational architecture is generativity-dominant: still-active goals around finishing her degree, mentoring granddaughters, preserving independence, and 'being remembered as someone who paid attention and showed up' (Q108, Q109).
